title: ArchPilot wire contract
description: Single source of truth for the shapes that cross the Python/TypeScript boundary. Build-scope decision D2 replaced the architects' shared `packages/core` with a Python backend, so nothing in the toolchain reconciles the two languages any more; this file is the replacement (decision D4). It covers (1) the ArchGraph shape shared by designs and patterns, and (2) three envelope rules, because the review of 2026-09-23 found that envelope drift - not graph drift - caused the first real bug. Validated by ArchPilot/backend/tests/test_contracts.py (jsonschema) and ArchPilot/src/contracts/contract.test.ts (ajv), both driven by fixtures/index.json. Deliberately NOT an OpenAPI document and deliberately not code-generated: at 2-4 users and one graph type a hand-maintained schema plus shared fixtures is right-sized.

camelCaseKey.title: Envelope rule (a) - wire casing
camelCaseKey.description: Every key that crosses the HTTP boundary is camelCase. The SPA's domain types are camelCase throughout (WorkspaceRecord.projectName, EntityEnvelope.schemaVersion, SizingResult.formulaVersion); Python is snake_case. The wire picks camelCase once, here. Backend side: app/schemas.py ApiModel sets alias_generator=to_camel.

camelCaseObject.description: Recursively asserts envelope rule (a) over a whole response body. Point any live API response at this to prove no snake_case key slipped in at any depth.

timestamp.title: Envelope rule (c) - timestamp format
timestamp.description: ISO 8601, always UTC, always with an explicit offset - `2026-09-23T06:26:52+00:00` or `2026-09-23T06:26:52Z`. A naive local timestamp is rejected: JavaScript's Date parses `2026-09-23 06:26:52` as local time and `2026-09-23T06:26:52` as UTC, so an offset-less string means two clients disagree about the same instant. Backend side: datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=0).isoformat().

errorResponse.title: Envelope rule (b) - error shape
errorResponse.description: Every non-2xx JSON body is exactly {detail} or {detail, requestId}. `detail` is a human-readable string, never an object or a list - FastAPI's default RequestValidationError body is a list and is normalised by app/main.py's exception handlers so this rule holds for 4xx as well as 5xx. `requestId` echoes the x-request-id response header so a user can quote one token in a bug report.

nodeType.description: Fixed palette (REQ-DESIGN-002). Adding a member is an additive, one-line edit here plus PALETTE in src/domain/graph.ts; that edit is the point of this file, not an obstacle to it. Renaming or removing one requires an ArchGraph schemaVersion bump.

props.description: The extension point (NFR-EXT-002). Adding a props key is additive and needs no change to this file; that is why the node object itself can afford to be closed.

label.description: REQ-DESIGN-003. Required as a key, may be empty: an unlabelled edge is a warning in validateGraph(), not a contract violation.

archGraph.title: ArchGraph - the one graph shape
archGraph.description: A user design and a reference pattern serialise to the identical document (architects' decision D1), which is what makes REQ-HUB-007 'apply to canvas' a deep copy with new IDs and REQ-HUB-008 'compare' a set diff. KNOWN LIMIT: JSON Schema cannot express referential integrity, so 'every edge.source names an existing node.id' and 'node ids are unique' are NOT checked here - they belong to validateGraph() in src/domain/graph.ts (task 1.5). This file checks shape; validateGraph() checks consistency.

schemaVersion.description: Pinned (NFR-EXT-002). Adding '1.1' here is the deliberate act that says a migration function exists in src/domain/graph.ts.
